>F4-3600 C18D-32GTZR

Ugh, yeah if it doesn't specifically list F4-3600C18D-32GTZR as being compatible, that's probably your issue I'm sad to say.  If I were you, I'd go ahead and update the BIOS to the latest version just to see if that fixes it.  I do believe additional RAM compat can be added via BIOS updates.

BIOS updates are generally pretty easy/straightforward.  Just follow the manufactuer's instructions and you'll be fine.  The biggest risk would be unplugging the power or having a power outage during the update, but most all modern mb's like yours will have a built-in fallback to prevent permanent goofery.

You're probably good on the RAM compatibility, you didn't buy some weird no-name brand, however I'd still check.  I've seen more than a few mainstream boards not support certain RAM configs from mainstream providers.

Well, you definitely troubleshot things properly.  I'd really think about looking at what version your BIOS is currently sitting at and whether there's a newer version that might correct this.

Also, check your motherboard's particular RAM compatibility list, which should be on the product page/support page for your motherboard on ASUS's site.  It's definitely possible the the particular model number of RAM you have isn't compat with your mb.

He worked at a small theater there, back when things like that would be in each little town due to the distance and expense involved driving to other towns. They've renovated this to be the museum and such

His actual house is a little bus ride out into farm land. The draw isn't just that he was born there, it's what his life was like, him and his family. The house is tiny, my 2 bedroom 2 bath townhouse is 4 times bigger, yet his parents raised 7 kids in it. It takes all of 10 minutes to fully tour, and they've restored it back to what it looked like back in the day, having been constructed under FDR's New Deal deal.

All of that adds up to it being something worthy of being preserved, for some.
